knowledge_point.title: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Simplify $\cos(x+30^\circ)-2\cos(x-30^\circ)$ using $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. Enter signed coefficients.

{{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=30^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x+30^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 30^\circ-\sin x\sin 30^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\sin x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\cos(u-v)=\cos u\cos v+\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=30^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x-30^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 30^\circ+\sin x\sin 30^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\sin x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Distribute the outside factors, then collect the sine and cosine terms. Let $E$ denote the original expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=1\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&\quad -2\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&=\left(1\cdot\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)+-2\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(1\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+-2\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=-\frac{3}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $- \frac{3}{2}$ and the second is $- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Simplify $2\cos(x-225^\circ)+2\cos(x+135^\circ)$ using $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. Enter signed coefficients.

{{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $\cos(u-v)=\cos u\cos v+\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=225^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x-225^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 225^\circ+\sin x\sin 225^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\sin x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=135^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x+135^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 135^\circ-\sin x\sin 135^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\sin x\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Distribute the outside factors, then collect the sine and cosine terms. Let $E$ denote the original expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&\quad +2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&=\left(2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=-2 \sqrt{2}\sin x-2 \sqrt{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $- 2 \sqrt{2}$ and the second is $- 2 \sqrt{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Simplify $2\cos(x+30^\circ)+\cos(x+330^\circ)$ using $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. Enter signed coefficients.

{{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=30^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x+30^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 30^\circ-\sin x\sin 30^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\sin x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=330^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x+330^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 330^\circ-\sin x\sin 330^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\sin x\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Distribute the outside factors, then collect the sine and cosine terms. Let $E$ denote the original expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&\quad +1\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&=\left(2\cdot\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)+1\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(2\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+1\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $- \frac{1}{2}$ and the second is $\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Simplify $2\cos(x-225^\circ)-2\cos(x-315^\circ)$ using $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. Enter signed coefficients.

{{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $\cos(u-v)=\cos u\cos v+\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=225^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x-225^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 225^\circ+\sin x\sin 225^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\sin x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\cos(u-v)=\cos u\cos v+\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=315^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x-315^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 315^\circ+\sin x\sin 315^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\sin x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Distribute the outside factors, then collect the sine and cosine terms. Let $E$ denote the original expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&\quad -2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&=\left(2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+-2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+-2\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=-2 \sqrt{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $0$ and the second is $- 2 \sqrt{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Simplify $2\cos(x+210^\circ)-\cos(x+150^\circ)$ using $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. Enter signed coefficients.

{{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=210^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x+210^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 210^\circ-\sin x\sin 210^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\sin x\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ with $u=x$ and $v=150^\circ$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos(x+150^\circ)&=\cos x\cos 150^\circ-\sin x\sin 150^\circ\\
&=\cos x\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\sin x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$

Distribute the outside factors, then collect the sine and cosine terms. Let $E$ denote the original expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=2\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&\quad -1\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x\right)\\
&=\left(2\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+-1\cdot\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(2\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+-1\cdot\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=\frac{3}{2}\sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}

The first blank is $\frac{3}{2}$ and the second is $- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
